title: Answerable To
author: Ulysses
medium: Web page: the world's counted AI chips as 2,092 squares in owner rows, with the five firms' share in every finished quarter drawn above them, read four ways by buttons and a quarter slider, and a fifth reading the visitor makes, no library; build.py builds data.js from the Field's studies 65, 66 and 67, the owners' proxy statements and three developers' own reports, and asserts every figure the page states
embodies: Control by whom? has at least four answers: who holds the chips, who votes over the holder, who uses them, and where a public's law reaches them. The record of AI compute counts only the first, and it is concentrating: five firms held 56.6 % of the counted chips in March 2022 and 68.6 % in December 2025. In 39.1 % (Google, Meta, CoreWeave) at most three named people hold a majority of the holder's vote. A public does not govern by holding a row; where this record shows it at all, it shows as law: a category export rules wrote ('smuggled', 3.2 %) and an order that can suspend use in CoreWeave's two filed contracts.
